headline: FBI warns AI pentest framework ARTEX automates global attacks, including ConnectWise supply-chain breach
summary: The FBI warns that attackers are using ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework, to automate attacks on organizations worldwide. The warning links the tool to a recent supply-chain breach at ConnectWise that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.

headline: Six unpatched flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers allow unauthenticated takeover
summary: Midnight Blue has disclosed six vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers that could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in. No patch is available, and firmware 5.4.0 does not fix the flaws. National cyber agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany have issued warnings to operators.

headline: NoisyTCP Linux kernel flaw allows remote crash of servers in default configurations
summary: Researchers have disclosed NoisyTCP, a Linux kernel vulnerability that has existed for about 11 years and affects almost all distributions. Attackers can use it to crash systems running Nginx, Apache or SSH servers with default settings. The source does not report a CVE identifier or any in-the-wild exploitation.

headline: Amazon reports attacker AI agents hunting exposed LiteLLM, Dify and One API apps for AI provider keys
summary: Amazon's threat intelligence team used decoy servers to capture records from attacker-run AI agents. The agents were searching internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API and Dify for stored AI provider API keys. According to the records, stolen keys were used to run the models that powered the search for more keys.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: BO Team used Log4Shell in VMware vCenter to compromise a Russian developer's code-signing server
summary: Kaspersky ICS CERT reports that BO Team (also called Black Owl or Hoody Hyena) had access to a Russian software developer's development infrastructure and code-signing server for months. The intrusion started through Log4Shell in VMware vCenter. The developer asked Kaspersky to investigate in June 2025. The source does not say whether any signed software was tampered with or shipped to customers.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: Honeypots record scans targeting chained LiteLLM/Starlette flaws CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710
summary: SANS ISC honeypots began receiving requests to the LiteLLM MCP REST endpoint /mcp-rest/test/tools/list over a weekend. The requests appear to be attempts to exploit CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. Horizon3.ai has described how chaining these flaws can give unauthenticated remote code execution. The source reports only scanning and exploit attempts. It does not confirm any successful compromise.

headline: Microsoft says outage was not a cyberattack and warns of phishing that exploits the incident
summary: Microsoft says a recent outage was not caused by a cyberattack. Phishing emails posing as Microsoft 365 service notices cited the real incident and threatened to delete held messages.

headline: Unpatched GeoVision camera software used to deploy cryptominers at 13 organizations
summary: Huntress reports that attackers used a GeoVision camera management service to get into Windows machines at 13 organizations and install cryptocurrency miners. Most of the intrusions happened between November 8 and 10, and the victims are in various industries. GeoVision has customers in 110 countries.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 95%; cross-industry relevance at least 60%

headline: FBI and Microsoft report AI platform ARTEX used in cyberattacks including on ConnectWise and Korean banks
summary: The FBI and Microsoft report that an AI platform called ARTEX was used in several cyberattacks. Reported targets include South Korean banks and the software company ConnectWise. The source excerpt does not give technical details, attribution or indicators.

headline: Attackers probe newly disclosed flaws in Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers
summary: VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB EVO controllers. Threat actors quickly began targeting two of them. The reporting describes probing attempts, and successful compromises have not been confirmed.

headline: FBI warns of growing criminal abuse of AI pentesting framework ARTEX
summary: The FBI reports that threat actors are increasingly using ARTEX, an open-source AI pentesting tool, to carry out fast, large-scale intrusions worldwide. The available summary names no specific victims or sectors.

headline: UnrealIRCd flaw CVE-2026-114713 exploited in attacks
summary: A high-severity UnrealIRCd vulnerability, CVE-2026-114713, is being exploited in attacks. It allows commands to be executed with server or IRCOp privileges.

headline: Microsoft reminds customers that Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in 60 days
summary: Microsoft has reminded customers again that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates when support ends in about two months. Organisations still running it will face growing unpatched exposure unless they migrate or buy extended updates.

headline: Microsoft issues emergency Windows updates to fix activation failures caused by monthly patches
summary: Microsoft has released emergency out-of-band updates. They fix Windows activation and licensing failures caused by this month's security updates.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 95%; cross-industry relevance at least 60%

headline: Microsoft warns of phishing campaign exploiting a global outage theme
summary: Microsoft has warned of a phishing campaign that uses a worldwide outage affecting the company and its users as a lure. The source gives few details about the campaign's targets or payloads.

headline: TSMC confirms employee personal data leak tied to cloud provider after 6.9GB auction listing
summary: TSMC confirmed that personal data about its employees leaked online. The leak followed a threat actor's auction of about 6.9GB of data allegedly stolen from the company, and reporting links the exposure to a cloud provider. The source excerpt gives no details on the cloud provider involved or the scope of the data.

headline: Forescout uses AI models to find 66 new flaws in TCP/IP stacks, including ones in unsupported devices
summary: Forescout researchers tested whether off-the-shelf AI models could find vulnerabilities on a small budget, using both source code and compiled binaries. They confirmed 99 flaws across 10 TCP/IP stacks. Of these, 66 were previously unknown, and about half of the new ones were rated high or critical. Some affect discontinued products that no vendor will patch. No exploitation was reported.

headline: Rspamd 4.3.0 fixes unauthenticated crash bugs and forged authentication-result bypass
summary: Rspamd 4.3.0 fixes bugs that let an unauthenticated attacker crash workers with a single malformed request or header. Other fixed bugs let forged authentication results pass through the filter. A separate milter proxy flaw affected versions 4.0.0 to 4.2.3, and forwarded mail could soften DMARC rejects.

headline: Google Project Zero plans to cut its disclosure deadline to 30 days by 2028
summary: Google Project Zero will move to publishing bug details 30 days after reporting them, whether or not a fix exists, by 2028. This could shorten the time defenders have to patch after vendor disclosures.

headline: UK ICO receives more than 300 reports of unauthorized insider access to medical records
summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office says it has received hundreds of reports this year of insiders viewing medical files without authorization. The figures point to an ongoing insider-risk problem in healthcare data handling.

headline: Criminal marketplace sells infostealer logs with AI-generated profiles of their victims
summary: Hudson Rock found an unnamed criminal marketplace selling infostealer logs bundled with AI-written profiles of each infected machine's owner. The profiles describe the owner's apparent employer and which accounts are worth buying. Buyers can search them in plain language.

headline: Google Project Zero moves to fixed disclosure deadlines, shrinking to 30 days by 2028
summary: Google Project Zero will now disclose bugs 90 days after reporting them to the vendor, whether or not a fix has shipped. This replaces the "90 + 30" rule. The deadline drops to 60 days on February 2, 2027 and to 30 days on January 3, 2028. Unpatched flaws may become public sooner, so patch cadence will come under pressure.

headline: REF3364 cryptomining operation uses SANSAR toolkit and modified NVIDIA library to hide GPU use
summary: A financially motivated activity cluster tracked as REF3364 runs a Linux cryptomining operation that tampers with the GPU readings defenders use to spot heavy workloads. Its Rust-based SANSAR orchestrator receives commands over Tor and manages both CPU and GPU miners.

headline: Anthropic Claude 5.2 models change handling of security tasks and bug-finding capability
summary: Anthropic has released Claude Mythos 5.2 to selected partners and Fable 5.2 to general users. Reporting says Fable 5.2 refuses fewer security-related tasks, while Mythos is better at finding vulnerabilities. This is a product change, not an incident.

headline: Microsoft previews Intune remote lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
summary: Microsoft is previewing an Intune feature that lets admins lock a lost, stolen or compromised Windows device without wiping it. The lock signs out all sessions, stays in place after restarts and while offline, and covers Windows 10/11 and Windows Server 2016–2022.

headline: uBlock Origin ad blocker flaw enables cross-site scripting
summary: A vulnerability in the widely used uBlock Origin ad blocker allows cross-site scripting, which could expose sensitive data. No exploitation was reported.

headline: Researchers demonstrate RCE in new Telegram widgets as Kaspersky suspects WebRAT delivery; Durov disputes the claims
summary: Researchers have demonstrated remote code execution through Telegram's newly launched widgets. Kaspersky suspects the widgets are being exploited to deliver WebRAT. Telegram founder Pavel Durov disputes the claims, so whether exploitation is happening remains unconfirmed.

headline: Uber breach at third-party provider exposes data of 150,000 people
summary: Attackers compromised a third-party service provider used by Uber and stole names, addresses and driver's license numbers. About 150,000 people are affected.

headline: Retadup worm resurfaces to distribute new CoffeeLoader variant, Kaspersky reports
summary: Kaspersky has analysed a new CoffeeLoader variant, a loader that delivers more malware, and links its spread to the Retadup worm. Retadup was taken down seven years ago. The infection chain uses an NSIS installer that drops a patched '7z.dll' file and runs it through rundll32.exe.

headline: Case study: phishing of luxury hotel reservation inboxes enabled fraudulent refunds
summary: Research describes attackers who used a fake booking request to get into luxury hotel reservation inboxes, then copied genuine refund requests to get fraudulent ones approved. It shows that "don't click links" advice fails for staff whose job is answering emails from strangers, and that splitting security between owner, operator and brand leaves no one accountable.

headline: Forescout says AI found 66 new vulnerabilities in 90 hours
summary: A Forescout report claims AI-assisted research found 66 new flaws in 90 hours, work it compares to nine months of manual effort. The excerpt does not name the affected products.

headline: Australian retailer Coles investigates cybersecurity incident
summary: Coles Group, Australia's second-largest retailer, is investigating a cybersecurity incident. The company says its stores have not been affected. Details of the incident's scope have not been disclosed.

headline: Tor 0.4.9.17 fixes security issues and IPv6 DoS-defense gap as relay attacks continue
summary: Tor 0.4.9.17 fixes several security issues, including one in how built-in DoS protections handle IPv6. The release comes during ongoing attacks on Tor relays.

headline: Trezor confirms hidden chip in third-party-sold crypto wallets that steals recovery words
summary: Trezor confirmed that some of its hardware wallets sold through a third party contained a hidden chip that steals recovery words. The excerpt does not say how many devices or which sales channel were affected.

headline: Cloudflare open-sources Kitesurf, its browser for AI agents, so it can be self-hosted
summary: Cloudflare has published the source code for Kitesurf, a browser that lets AI agents load web pages and run their JavaScript on Cloudflare Workers without a full desktop browser. Developers can inspect it, change it, test it locally and deploy their own copy.

headline: Sponsored piece promotes unified exposure management approach
summary: This is a sponsored article that argues for unified exposure management. The approach combines asset visibility, attacker-based prioritization and remediation. It contains no new threat or vulnerability information.

headline: YARA-X 1.23.0 released with 4 improvements and 16 bug fixes
summary: YARA-X version 1.23.0 is out with four improvements and 16 bug fixes. The source does not mention any security fixes.

headline: Sponsored piece on threat management strategy for frontier AI
summary: This sponsored content argues that organizations need to rethink security to address vulnerabilities in frontier AI. It reports no specific incident or vulnerability.

headline: Sponsored survey: practitioners plan to give AI more SOC autonomy but containment trust lags
summary: A sponsored survey finds that 91% of security practitioners plan to give AI more autonomy in 2027. The piece argues that AI-led containment needs more groundwork than AI-assisted detection before it can be trusted.

headline: Datasette 0.65.6 backports fix for unauthorized database download via custom routes
summary: Datasette 0.65.6 backports a minor security fix from 1.0a43. Before the fix, users who had been denied access could download a database registered with a route that differs from its name.

headline: Datasette 1.0a43 adds streaming output and fixes private stored query exposure
summary: The Datasette 1.0a43 alpha adds streaming output renderers and UI improvements. It also includes security fixes, one of which has a GitHub advisory: the title and SQL of private stored queries could be exposed, though the queries themselves could not be executed.

headline: Ory Hydra open-source OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect server profiled
summary: Ory Hydra is an open-source OAuth 2.0 server and OpenID Connect provider. It issues and validates tokens, registers client applications and manages signing keys. It does not store user credentials, so logins stay with an organization's existing identity system.

headline: EFF argues tech companies are reshaping the meaning of privacy through invasive gadgets
summary: The EFF says tech companies keep releasing gadgets that undermine the privacy of users and the people around them. It describes this as an attempt to change how privacy itself is understood. The piece is commentary and has no direct operational impact.

headline: ESET Mobile Security for iOS adds phishing link checks and device security scans
summary: ESET's iOS app checks suspicious links, reviews device settings and permissions, and assesses Wi-Fi connections. It supports iOS 18.0 and later, and the free features need no account.

headline: Tor network hit by weeks-long DDoS attack; update intended to mitigate it
summary: For several weeks, the Tor network has been under a large DDoS attack that is overloading its servers. An update is expected to help relieve the problem.

headline: Datasette releases MapLibre geospatial plugin built largely with an AI coding assistant
summary: A new alpha Datasette plugin, datasette-maplibre, adds MapLibre GL and OpenFreeMap mapping for GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points. The author says most of it was generated from a single prompt to an AI model. The item has no security content.
